extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users / pgf (TikZ) package users and TeX developers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implementation details for using pgf's calendar, page-management (pgfpages), extended color (xxcolor) and mathematical engine facilities. Covers available macros, expected behaviors, options, and recommended usage/workarounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarifdate* date-info macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros provide detailed info about the date being tested: \pgfcalendarifdatejulian (Julian day), \pgfcalendarifdateweekday (weekday), \pgfcalendarifdateyear (year), \pgfcalendarifdatemonth (month), \pgfcalendarifdateday (day of month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these macros inside key code or tests to inspect the date to be checked. Example: define a key that sets \pgfcalendarmatchestrue when \pgfcalendarifdatemonth=5 and \pgfcalendarifdateday=1 to detect Workers day. The new key may set the TeX-if \ifpgfcalendarmatches to true (if it is already true, no action should be taken).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define new date-test keys by setting \pgfcalendarmatchestrue
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing a new key for \pgfcalendar that performs a test, the key may set the TeX-if \ifpgfcalendarmatches to true to indicate that the date passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key code needs the date info (available via macros above). Example provided: \define@key{pgfcalendar}{workers day}[] { \ifnum\pgfcalendarifdatemonth=5\relax \ifnum\pgfcalendarifdateday=1\relax \pgfcalendarmatchestrue \fi \fi }

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarweekdayname / \pgfcalendarweekdayshortname / \pgfcalendarmonthname / \pgfcalendarmonthshortname
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands expand to textual (or abbreviated) names of weekdays or months given a numeric index, e.g., \pgfcalendarweekdayname{0} -> Monday (in English), \pgfcalendarweekdayshortname{2} -> Wed, \pgfcalendarmonthname{12} -> December, \pgfcalendarmonthshortname{12} -> Dec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands respect localization (see localization entry). Use them to produce human-readable names inside calendars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of textual date names
rubrics_metrics.description: All textual representations of week days or months are wrapped with \translate commands from the translator package; if translator is not loaded, no translation takes place. pgfcalendar will try to load translator-months-dictionary if translator is loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have dates translated to the current language, load the translator package and appropriate dictionaries. If translator not loaded, strings remain in the default language.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendar command contract
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfcalendar{prefix}{start date}{end date}{rendering code} enumerates each date in the given range and executes rendering code with macros set up for the current date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rendering code must perform the actual typesetting and positioning (e.g., placing nodes). Calls of rendering code are not surrounded by TeX groups, so settings can accumulate between iterations (useful but be aware of side effects). The macro need not be inside a pgfpicture; it can be used in normal TeX or with other packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macros available inside rendering code (current-date info)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside rendering code the following macros are available: \pgfcalendarprefix, \pgfcalendarbeginiso, \pgfcalendarbeginjulian, \pgfcalendarendiso, \pgfcalendarendjulian, \pgfcalendarcurrentjulian, \pgfcalendarcurrentweekday (0=Monday), \pgfcalendarcurrentyear, \pgfcalendarcurrentmonth (two digits), \pgfcalendarcurrentday (two digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to adapt rendering per-day (positioning, formatting, conditional styling). Note month/day are two-digit strings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifdate convenience conditional inside \pgfcalendar
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifdate{tests}{code}{else code} performs the same effect as calling \pgfcalendarifdate for the current date inside a \pgfcalendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \ifdate to test common predicates (e.g., Sunday, weekend, day of month=1) for simpler conditional rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarshorthand representations
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfcalendarshorthand{kind}{representation} expands to a representation of the current day/month/year/day-of-week depending on kind (d, m, y, w). Representations: '-', '=', '0', '.', 't'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meanings: '-' selects shortest numerical (no leading zeros); '=' selects shortest numerical but adds a space to single-digit days/months; '0' selects two-digit numeric for days/months; 't' textual; '.' abbreviated textual. Recommended: locally do \let\%=\pgfcalendarshorthand so you can write \%wt etc. Examples: ISO form 2007-01-20 as \%y0-\%m0-\%d0 and long form uses \%wt, \%mt \%d-, \%y0.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfcalendarsuggestedname node-naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfcalendarsuggestedname expands to the calendar prefix followed by a hyphen followed by the ISO format date (prefix empty -> empty string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this suggested name as node names for day nodes so they follow a consistent scheme like mycal-2007-01-01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: pgfpages and hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Using pgfpages will 'destroy' hyperlinks in the sense that hyperlinks will appear at incorrect positions in final output because PDF hyperlink bounding rectangles are in absolute page coordinates and are not affected by transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fundamental PDF limitation; do not expect transformations applied by pgfpages to be applied to hyperlink coordinates. No current workaround is promised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic usage of pgfpages and layouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfpagesuselayout{layout}[options] to install a pre-defined layout (e.g., '2 on 1') and options like paper size, orientation, border shrink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \pgfpagesuselayout{2 on 1}[a4paper,landscape,border shrink=5mm] will put two logical pages on a physical A4 landscape page and shrink logical pages to leave a 5mm border. Layout selection is the primary user-level mechanism for multi-page arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beamer/logical-page orientation interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: When logical pages are already landscape (e.g., beamer frames), do not add the 'landscape' option when using some layouts; orientation of resulting physical pages depends on logical page orientation and the chosen layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., for beamer use \pgfpagesuselayout{2 on 1}[a4paper,border shrink=5mm] (no landscape). For 4 on 1 you may need landscape, for 8 on 1 you must not, for 16 on 1 you need it again — check orientation logic per layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-number/.aux file problem and workaround
rubrics_metrics.description: Using pgfpages can produce wrong page numbers in the .aux file because TeX writes page numbers to .aux only when the physical page is shipped out; pgfpages changes shipment order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workaround: typeset once without \pgfpagesuselayout (comment it out), then rerun TeX with \pgfpagesuselayout included and add \nofiles to prevent modifying the .aux file. Example given with two-step process: first normal typeset (layout commented), then typeset with layout and \nofiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: resize to layout options and physical paper size specifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'resize to' layout fits logical pages to a specified physical size. Options: physical paper height/width=(size), a0paper..a6paper, letterpaper, legalpaper, executivepaper, landscape, border shrink=(size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to adapt documents prepared for one paper size (e.g., letter) to another (e.g., A4) by resizing logical pages without changing original page breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined layout behaviors and options (2 on 1, 4 on 1, 8 on 1, 16 on 1, rounded corners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of how many logical pages are placed per physical page and additional options such as 'odd numbered pages right' for 2 on 1 and 'corner width' for rounded corners. Rounded corners requires logical pages to fill their background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the layout that matches desired packing; if using 'rounded corners' ensure each logical page fills its background or corners will clip wrong regions. Use 'odd numbered pages right' to control whether first page goes on right when using 2 on 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-screen layouts and their options
rubrics_metrics.description: 'two screens with lagging second' places two logical pages side-by-side, the second showing what the main page showed on the previous physical page; options: second right/left/top/bottom to place the lagging second page accordingly. 'two screens with optional second' updates the second only when explicit commands are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These layouts are useful for dual-projector setups. For 'optional second' use \pgfshipoutlogicalpage{2}{box} or \pgfcurrentpagewillbelogicalpage{2} to control updates to the second screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpagesdeclarelayout lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfpagesdeclarelayout{layout}{before actions}{after actions} predefines a layout. On \pgfpagesuselayout: before actions executed, then \setkeys{pgfpagesuselayoutoption}{options}, then after actions executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to define custom reusable layouts. The 'before' phase can set defaults; 'after' phase assembles physical/logical page options (see example for 'resize to').

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpagesphysicalpageoptions settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Options that set characteristics of the physical page such as logical pages=(n), first logical shipout, last logical shipout, current logical shipout, physical height=(height), physical width=(width).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: logical pages defines total logical pages; first/last define interval used to store shipped pages; current logical shipout can 'warp' the next logical page to fill. physical height/width typically differ from \paperheight/\paperwidth used during typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpageslogicalpageoptions per-logical-page settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-logical-page options include center=(pgf point), resized width=(size), resized height=(size), original width/height, scale, xscale, yscale, rotation, copy from=(logical page), border shrink=(size), border code=(code), corner width=(size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to position and scale each logical page on the physical page. copy from retains or duplicates contents across physical shipouts; border code runs before inserting the page with a path installed (e.g., use \pgfstroke to draw a rectangle); xscale/yscale can flip pages with factor -1. When resized width and height both given, scaling chosen to meet both while preserving aspect ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of 'copy from' and persistence of logical pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally logical pages are voided after a physical shipout, but copy from=(n) causes the current logical page to be filled with contents of old logical page n, enabling retained or repeated displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use copy from to make logical pages retain prior contents or to have one logical page show what another showed on the just-shipped-out physical page (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Border code usage and path coordinate system
rubrics_metrics.description: border code=(code) executes code before inserting the page box with a path preinstalled that is a rectangle around the logical page; coordinates are set so rectangle starting at origin with TEX-box 0 height/width fills the logical page exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to draw frames, rounded corners, or decorative borders. Example: \pgfpageslogicalpageoptions{1}{border code=\pgfstroke} draws a rectangle around the logical page. You can call \pgfdiscardpath and construct your own path; the logical page is inserted after the code runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How logical pages are created and alternative ways to set them
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical pages are created when TeX performs a \shipout; pgfpages intercepts \shipout and stores the page in an internal box until enough logical pages accumulate for a physical shipout. Alternative ways to set logical page contents: \pgfpagesshipoutlogicalpage{number}box and \pgfpagescurrentpagewillbelogicalpage{number}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \pgfpagesshipoutlogicalpage sets a logical page explicitly using a TeX box and does not affect the logical-page counter nor cause a physical shipout (useful to set pages normally not filled). \pgfpagescurrentpagewillbelogicalpage interrupts the normal order so the current TeX page will become the given logical page number when shipped out.

rubrics_metrics.name: xxcolor: \begin{colormixin}{mix-in specification} environment semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A mix-in specification is 'number!' followed by a color name (number between 0 and 100). The mix-in is applied to all colors inside the environment; the number states what percentage of the desired color should be used, the rest mixed with the mix-in color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 90!blue mixes in 10% blue into everything (i.e., uses 90% of the specified color, 10% blue); 25!white makes colors nearly white. At environment start the current color is also mixed. Nested colormixin environments append mix-ins; use \colorcurrentmixin to inspect the accumulated mix-ins. Note: only colors set via \color are affected; colors inside images are not changed unless alternative images with mix-in suffixes are provided (see \pgfuseimage behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfuseimage behavior inside colormixin
rubrics_metrics.description: When \pgfuseimage{foo} is called inside a colormixin with parameter like 50!black, the command checks for an image named foo.!50!black and uses it if present; nested mix-ins append suffixes (e.g., foo.!50!white!25!black).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support washed-out/dimmed variants of images, supply alternate image files named with the mix-in suffixes expected; otherwise images remain unchanged inside the colormixin environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: \colorcurrentmixin expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \colorcurrentmixin expands to the current accumulated mix-in string (e.g., '!75!white' or '!50!white!75!black!75!white').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to debug or inspect current mix-ins or to build image names for \pgfuseimage lookups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical engine capabilities and loading
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf's mathematical engine supports integer and non-integer arithmetic, units, functions (sqrt, sin, cos), and pseudo-random numbers; it can be used standalone. Load with \usepackage{pgfmath} (LaTeX), \input pgfmath.tex (plain TeX) or \usemodule[pgfmath] (ConTeXt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The engine defines commands like \pgfmathparse and calc-like wrappers (for dimension/counter setting). It's implicitly used when pgf parses numbers/dimensions in higher-level macros (e.g., \pgfpoint{2cm+4cm/2}{3cm*sin(30)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical engine layering
rubrics_metrics.description: The engine is structured into layers: (1) Top layer exposing \pgfmathparse and wrappers; (2) Calculation layer providing macros for specific computations; (3) Implementation layer providing actual implementations that can be changed without affecting higher layers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the top layer for normal parsing; implementation details can be optimized or swapped by advanced users by altering lower layers.
